key_insight: PanoLOG makes large-scale outdoor 3D reconstruction practical with panoramic images by replacing camera-frustum-based partitioning with geometry- and gradient-aware scene partitioning. This preserves efficient block-wise training even when every panorama sees nearly the whole scene.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the high data-collection and computation cost of scaling 3D Gaussian Splatting to large outdoor environments. It specifically solves the failure of existing partitioning methods under 360° equirectangular panoramic imagery, where omnidirectional visibility turns local optimization into near-global training.
method: Uses panoramic equirectangular images to reduce capture effort while retaining full-scene coverage.
Introduces a two-stage coarse-to-fine framework called PanoLOG for outdoor reconstruction.
Partitions the scene using geometry and gradient signals instead of relying on local camera frustums that do not exist in panoramic setups.
impact: This approach makes panoramic 3D reconstruction more scalable and efficient for real-world outdoor scenes. For practitioners, it offers a way to lower capture cost and keep optimization tractable without sacrificing coverage.
